source: accepted knowledge decisions plus current prose drafts

chapters.title: The Invitation
chapters.summary: Royal herald Gaston invites the Dragon Rider Order to the Grand Tourney in Bellacourt. Alaric leads a six-rider delegation consisting of Alaric, Gawain, Caradoc and three additional Dragon Rider Knights, while Percival remains in the Valley to command the Order.

chapters.title: Audience with King Charles
chapters.summary: The delegation reaches Bellacourt and encounters the Kingdom of Bretonnia within the wider, politically fragmented Bretonnian Lands. King Charles III presents his idealistic project of greater unity, while Archbishop Anselm and the Church distrust the unfamiliar dragons and require them to return to the Valley.

chapters.title: The Vigil and the Knighting
chapters.summary: The riders observe pages, squires, knightly vigil and accolade, learning the spiritual and social ideals of Bretonnian chivalry while Alaric notices the tensions between noble duty, hereditary privilege and merit.

chapters.title: Their First Jousting
chapters.summary: Without their dragons, the riders train as horsemen and jousters at the Royal Fields. Master Bertrand teaches them that battlefield skill does not automatically translate to tournament skill, while heraldry introduces how medieval identity, allegiance, history and ideals are displayed. Alaric's exact personal heraldry remains deliberately unresolved.

chapters.title: The Capital Markets
chapters.summary: Alaric explores Bellacourt's farmers, merchants and guilds and sees how privileges are paired with obligations. He also begins to understand the Church as a practical institution woven into urban welfare and social responsibility, just before news arrives of a water-borne sickness in western communities.

chapters.title: Archbishop Anselm's Quest
chapters.summary: The Church coordinates practical relief across lordship boundaries while Alaric and the Dragon Riders recover the Chalice of Saint Armand from a remote abbey abandoned after a landslide. The ruined complex combines spider-infested halls with deeper sacred stone guardians and escalating trials or puzzles. The Chalice genuinely purifies contaminated wells and cisterns, causing new cases of sickness to decline, while the mission deepens Alaric's understanding of the Church without yet resolving the dispute over dragons.

chapters.title: The Feast and the Conspiracy
chapters.summary: A royal feast celebrates the relic's return and renewed tournament festivities. Alaric discovers Count Bernier's conspiracy against Charles and overhears that Bernier is cooperating with the external warlord Lothar. The plot erupts into open action when Bernier's network moves against the court.

chapters.title: Rescue Mission
chapters.summary: Bernier's conspirators kidnap Lord Raymond, Charles III's cousin and heir-presumptive, as a primary attempt to gain leverage over the king and destabilize the succession. With the dragons back in the Valley, Alaric and the riders pursue by horse and rescue Raymond before he can be delivered into Bernier's wider scheme.

chapters.title: Attack!
chapters.summary: The failed kidnapping does not halt the parallel military operation already prepared by Bernier and Lothar. Sabotaged warnings, false orders and compromised local defenses allow Lothar's army to approach Bellacourt unexpectedly. Charles, Raymond and Alaric return before the encirclement closes and become trapped inside the capital. As the siege tightens, Martin breaks out as courier toward the Valley to request Dragon Rider relief.

chapters.title: Breaking the Siege
chapters.summary: After roughly three days of urgent courier travel and a rapid Dragon Rider mobilization led from the Valley by Percival, the relief force flies toward Bellacourt, with the dragon journey taking roughly one and a half to two days. The dragons break Lothar's siege and save the capital. Their conduct and sacrifice force Archbishop Anselm and the Church to reconsider their inherited judgment and publicly accept the dragons as defenders rather than monsters.

chapters.title: Honor and Reward
chapters.summary: After the victory, the Church publicly recognizes the dragons and the Dragon Rider Order. Charles III grants the Order a modest but real feudal holding in Bretonnia: a fortified manor-house with a defensive tower, dependent lands and limited vassals or tenant households, together with river, woodland, fishing, timber and hunting rights. The holding becomes a permanent Dragon Rider chapter house and foothold in the Bretonnian Lands without making the Order a major territorial power.
